source.snippet: I think at this point if someone charges 50% upfront of what hypothetically they could make from all the bloat people would pay for it. If a smart TV costs 500$ and each TV makes them 400$ in 10 years then charging 700$ sans smart features would sell if they advertised it that way.

problem_statement: Privacy-conscious consumers cannot easily buy a high-quality display without embedded smart TV surveillance software and ad-delivery systems; they are forced to choose between picture quality and data privacy.
target_segment: Privacy-conscious consumers and households willing to pay a premium for surveillance-free home entertainment hardware
notes: Single HN comment but the logic is sound and recurring — commenter explicitly models the willingness-to-pay ('charging 700$ sans smart features would sell'). Weak buyer signal (single point, no business context) but the consumer has money and articulates a price. Potential product: a curated reseller or hardware mod service that ships de-bloated displays with a privacy guarantee, sold at a transparent premium. Signal strength kept low (2) due to single data point and hobbyist/consumer framing.
